definitions.explanation: A hot pepper of the genus Capsicum, used widely in Japanese cooking as a spice. Includes both fresh and dried forms.

examples.japanese: {唐辛子|とうがらし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{入|い}れ→入れる：01098_ireru⟧すぎた。
examples.english: I put in too much chili pepper.

examples.japanese: ⟦うどん→うどん：05182_udon⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{七味唐辛子|しちみとうがらし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かけて→かける：00854_kakeru⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: I eat udon topped with seven-spice chili powder.

examples.japanese: ⟦{庭|にわ}→庭：02239_niwa⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{唐辛子|とうがらし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{栽培|さいばい}して→栽培する：09860_saibaisuru⟧、⟦{乾燥|かんそう}→乾燥：00184_kansou⟧⟦させて→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{保存|ほぞん}→保存：03626_hozon⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I grow chili peppers in my garden, dry them, and store them.

notes:
The name literally means 'Tang (Chinese) mustard child,' reflecting its historical import route. In everyday usage, {唐辛子|とうがらし} can refer to both fresh chili peppers and dried/powdered chili. {七味唐辛子|しちみとうがらし} (seven-spice chili powder) and ⟦{一味唐辛子|いちみとうがらし}→一味唐辛子：19042_ichimitougarashi⟧ (pure chili powder) are common condiments on Japanese dining tables.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{七味|しちみ}→七味：20131_shichimi⟧{唐辛子|とうがらし} — seven-spice chili powder
- ⟦{一味|いちみ}→一味：11238_ichimi⟧{唐辛子|とうがらし} — pure chili powder
- {鷹|たか}の{爪|つめ} — dried whole red chili (lit. hawk's claw)
- {唐辛子|とうがらし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{効|き}かせる→効く：01932_kiku⟧ — to add chili spiciness
